🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-winning actress whose first film role in "On the Waterfront" put her on the map and who went on to star opposite Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock's "North by Northwest," has died at 102.

Saint died of natural causes on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at her home in Los Angeles, "surrounded by family and loved ones," her representative Jeff Sanderson confirmed to USA TODAY.

Born July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey, Saint won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her very first film role — Edie Doyle opposite Marlon Brando in Elia Kazan's "On the Waterfront" (1954). She had given birth to her son just two days before the win and began her acceptance speech by saying, "I may have the baby right here!"

Five years later she remade her screen persona as the cool, enigmatic spy Eve Kendall opposite Cary Grant in Hitchcock's "North by Northwest" (1959), one of the most celebrated thrillers ever made.

Saint's career spanned seven decades, from the infancy of live television in postwar New York — where she was among its pioneering stars — through film and stage, earning an Emmy in 1990 for the miniseries "People Like Us" and voicing the elder Katara in "The Legend of Korra." In 1960 she became one of the few actresses to be given two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, for motion pictures and television.

After Olivia de Havilland's death in July 2020, Saint held the title of the oldest living Academy Award winner and one of the last living links to Hollywood's golden age. She celebrated her 102nd birthday on July 4, 2026, with four generations of family.

Saint married producer and director Jeffrey Hayden in 1951; they were married for 65 years until his death in 2016. She is survived by her two children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

Sources: statement from representative Jeff Sanderson to USA TODAY; obituary reporting.

title: Beyond the 956: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar-winning star of 'On the Waterfront,' dies at 102
